newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop to new 1997 low, outlook gloomy.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop to new 1997 low, outlook gloomy.

text.p: Thai stocks plummeted to their lowest level so far this year in thin, pre-holiday trade on Monday and analysts said the outlook for the battered market in the near term was gloomy.
The market shrugged off news that three local banks had made small cuts in lending rates after strong signals from the Bank of Thailand encouraging easing of high local rates.

The index fell to a new 1997 low of 672.48 points, down 11.52, the lowest close since March 6 when it ended at 676.65. Brokers blamed the fall on local mutual fund selling of large capitalised stocks ahead of public holidays on May 1 and 5.
Thai Farmers Bank Plc, Siam Commercial Bank Plc and Krung Thai Bank Plc all announced 25 basis point cut in their minimum lending rates (MLR) from April 29.
The changes brought the MLR at Krungthai Bank to 12.75 percent and to 13.00 percent at the other two banks.

"There are signs that the stock index would drop further from Monday because of investor concerns about interest rates remaining high," said Witawus Charuchandr, analyst at Ekachart Finance and Securities Plc.
He added that the market was disappointed because it had expected deeper rate cuts.
Generally, analysts expected rates to fall by 50-100 basis points and said even that would be enough only to relieve the slowing Thai economy and indebted businesses, not revive them.

"Ideally investors want to see between 1.0-2.0 (percentage points) rate cuts. I think its difficult. The index will continue to fall but I don't want to say when it will hit the bottom," Witawus said.

The Thai stock market has fallen by nearly 50 percent over the past year on negative sentiment, mainly about poor quality loans of troubled finance companies, and the woes of depressed and cash-strapped property firms.
George Morgan, head of the foreign brokers association, and director and country manager of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett Asia said the market could head lower before recovering in the future.

"I think we will probably have a rebound from an oversold position. But because people are gradually writing off this years earnings, and are not very confident about next year's, it will probably go to lower lows from one of these rebounds and could easily hit 600, or even break through that," he added.
"The feeling among the foreign brokers is bit mixed. Several people have already pinned their colours to the overweight mast but those calls so far appear to be a little early," he said.
Morgan noted that because of Thai economic policies gave high priority to the exchange rate policy it could mean rates could only come down slowly.
The Thai baht was weaker late on Monday but traders said that was because of the strong dollar overseas rather than the news of small rate cuts.
The currency was quoted in a narrow range of 26.102 to 26.133 against the greenback, near the baht midrate set by the central bank at 26.11 to the dollar on Monday.
